reason: Same problem, same region already exists: a tier-A 2024/2025 paper detects and dates PMFBY prevented/failed sowing status from satellite time series in coastal India at 92.3% accuracy. It doesn't cover flood-shock or recovery milestones and uses raw SAR, not embeddings, so this isn't fully closed, but it kills the 'nobody has tried event-dating for PMFBY' framing. KrishiRakshak (NDVI+GBM) also targets PMFBY eligibility timing. The candidate must beat these, not just exist alongside AlphaEarth's annual layer.

prior_art.title: Early season prevented and failed rice sowing detection using temporal Synthetic Aperture Radar data in coastal India for crop insurance applications
prior_art.why: Same problem (dating PMFBY-relevant sowing failure) and same region (coastal India) at 92.3% accuracy, but uses raw Sentinel-1 SAR, not embeddings, and does not touch flood-shock or recovery milestones, so it narrows rather than fully closes the candidate.

prior_art.why: Same problem framing (PMFBY damage/eligibility assessment) and same region, but classifies eligibility at a point in time rather than dating a sequence of sowing/flood/recovery milestones, and does not use satellite embeddings.

prior_art.why: Establishes YES-TECH as the mandated government yield-estimation stack (SAR/optical + weather models); it is a yield estimator, not an event-date auditor, but is the deployed incumbent this candidate would have to interoperate with or displace.

prior_art.title: Introducing Custom Satellite Embeddings, powered by AlphaEarth Foundations
prior_art.why: Confirms the on-demand monthly embedding capability the candidate relies on exists as a general-purpose product, but shows no agriculture-insurance or India case study, so it is enabling infrastructure, not competing prior art.

prior_art.title: Satellite Solutions For Agricultural Insurance — EOSDA
prior_art.why: Generic NDVI-based crop-insurance monitoring product, not India-PMFBY-specific and not embeddings-based; shows the crop-insurance-satellite category is crowded but does not close the event-dating delta.

type_b_fields.measurable_axis: Accuracy of dating the insurance event (sowing failure / flood / recovery) vs PMFBY cutoffs, benchmarked against the SAR paper's 92.3% P/FS detection accuracy.
type_b_fields.attributable_to: Using on-demand monthly multi-sensor Custom Satellite Embeddings to date three event types per season, vs a bespoke single-sensor SAR threshold pipeline built only for pre-season sowing failure.

nearest_neighbours_do_not: The SAR P/FS paper does not use foundation-model embeddings and does not date flood-shock or recovery milestones, only a single pre-season binary status. KrishiRakshak does not do temporal event-dating, only point-in-time eligibility classification, and is Sentinel-2 NDVI+GBM, not embeddings. Neither compares monthly on-demand embeddings against annual AlphaEarth layers.
notes: No product or paper found that specifically applies AlphaEarth/Custom Satellite Embeddings to PMFBY auditing; that combination looks open. The risk is entirely that the *problem* (PMFBY event-date audit) already has a working tier-A solution in the exact region, just via a different (SAR) method.
